items.answer: Give the analyst's client list a badge that shows each client's Watchlist level, WL 1 to WL 4, each in its brand colour. Success is REQ-UI-01's AC: wlBadgeHtml(1..4) returns the badge for that level and any other value throws a RangeError, with the stylesheet following the brand standard (BV-colours, BV-type, BV-contrast, BV-shape, BV-voice).
items.quote: The analyst's client list shows each client's Watchlist level (WL 1–4). Build the badge that shows it.

items.answer: The analyst, who sees the badge in the client list. The badge is display only; no role-based visibility in this slice (the client list is out of scope).
items.quote: The analyst's client list shows each client's Watchlist level

items.answer: In scope: web/wlBadge.mjs exporting wlBadgeHtml(level), web/wlBadge.css (one class per level) and tests under test/ run by node --test. Out of scope: the client list itself, persistence, how the level is computed. web/tokens.css is not modified.
items.quote: Out of scope: the client list itself, persistence, and how the level is computed.

items.answer: Yes. wlBadgeHtml(n) === 'WL n' for n=1..4; 0, 5, -1, 1.5, NaN, Infinity, '1', null, undefined and no argument each throw a RangeError. In web/wlBadge.css .wl-badge--N sets its background to var(--wl-N); text var(--on-wl), font var(--font-sans), radius var(--radius-pill), padding var(--space-1) calc(var(--space-1) * 2). No hex, rgb(), hsl() or colour name in wlBadge.css or wlBadge.mjs.
items.quote: any other value throws a RangeError

items.answer: No contradiction in the request. CLAUDE.md defines WL as 0–4 but the request covers 1–4 and says any other value throws, so wlBadgeHtml(0) throws (request wins). README says code lives in src/<area>/ but the contract puts the badge in web/ (request wins).
items.quote: any other value throws a RangeError

items.answer: One requirement, REQ-UI-01, Must; one task.
items.quote: UI slice, 1 task

items.answer: web/wlBadge.mjs provides wlBadgeHtml(level); only the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 are valid. Returns exactly 'WL ' + level + '' (one space, no other attributes, no surrounding whitespace). CSS classes .wl-badge and .wl-badge--1..4.
items.quote: wlBadgeHtml(level) → WL

items.answer: Any value other than 1, 2, 3 or 4 throws a RangeError (instance of RangeError). No fallback, no empty string. Includes 0, 5, -1, 1.5, NaN, Infinity, numeric strings, null, undefined, missing argument.
items.quote: any other value throws a RangeError

items.answer: Nothing to stay compatible with: web/ holds only tokens.css, src/ and test/ only .gitkeep.
A small UI module (function + stylesheet) inside the existing single-repo POC; no service.
items.quote: web/wlBadge.mjs — wlBadgeHtml(level) … web/wlBadge.css — the badge's styles

items.answer: One component wl-badge (web): web/wlBadge.mjs, web/wlBadge.css, tests under test/web/. Owner frontend, reviewer reviewer. web/tokens.css consumed, not changed.
items.quote: tests with node --test under test/

items.answer: Yes, a web UI fragment: an HTML string (span) plus a stylesheet, rendered by the future client list. Plain ESM and plain CSS, no framework.
items.quote: web/wlBadge.css — the badge's styles (one class per level).

items.answer: Presentation layer: a pure function mapping a level to badge HTML, plus CSS. No BFF, middleware, core service or API.
items.quote: Out of scope: the client list itself, persistence, and how the level is computed.

items.answer: JavaScript on Node.js 18+ as ES modules (.mjs) plus plain CSS; node:test + node:assert/strict.
items.quote: Plain Node ESM, no dependencies

items.answer: No new dependencies; Node built-ins only.

items.answer: No store; the level is an argument and persistence is out of scope.

items.answer: No external systems are called.

items.answer: No web framework: a plain string and plain CSS. Design system = the brand standard + web/tokens.css. No state. Dark mode: no.
items.quote: Plain Node ESM, no dependencies

items.answer: WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, 4.5:1, between var(--on-wl) and each var(--wl-1..4); all pass (see X-contrast). Visible text 'WL n' carries the level, so colour is not the only cue. Not interactive; the contract fixes the markup, so no aria attributes are added. Role a11y is on the job.
items.quote: Text and its background meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (4.5:1 for normal text).

items.answer: No localisation: fixed label 'WL ' + digit 1–4; no locale formats, no RTL.
items.quote: the text "WL 1" … "WL 4"

items.answer: No screen designs; the brand standard decides: WL N background var(--wl-N), text var(--on-wl), font var(--font-sans), radius var(--radius-pill), padding var(--space-1) vertical and calc(var(--space-1) * 2) horizontal, dark mode no. Loading/empty/error states do not apply (invalid input throws).
items.quote: Watchlist level colours: WL 1 → var(--wl-1), WL 2 → var(--wl-2), WL 3 → var(--wl-3), WL 4 → var(--wl-4); the text on every level badge is var(--on-wl).

items.answer: No target stated; pure constant-time string function.
No auth or secrets. Only 1–4 accepted, else RangeError; the output never contains caller-supplied text, so no injection path.
items.quote: any other value throws a RangeError

items.answer: No personal data; only a level number.
Nothing to audit; the badge only renders.
The brand standard (BV-colours, BV-type, BV-contrast, BV-shape, BV-voice) binds: no colour value outside web/tokens.css, including wlBadge.css, wlBadge.mjs and test files. No domain regulation named.
items.quote: no colour value (hex, rgb, hsl or a colour name) is written in any other file.

items.answer: node:test + node:assert/strict via node --test in test/web/. Unit: exact strings 1–4; RangeError for 0, 5, -1, 1.5, NaN, '1', null, undefined, none; CSS read as text: .wl-badge--N uses var(--wl-N), base uses var(--on-wl), var(--font-sans), var(--radius-pill), the stated padding; no colour literals in wlBadge.css/.mjs. Any contrast check reads values from web/tokens.css. No browser test.
items.quote: tests with node --test under test/

items.answer: node --test must pass (verify_full). No lint/typecheck/scans configured.
items.quote: tests with node --test under test/

items.question: How is the badge delivered and consumed? Is it only merged to main of the POC repo for a later client-list slice to import, or must it be served or published somewhere now?
options: A: merged to main only, no deployment; a later client-list slice imports web/wlBadge.mjs and links web/tokens.css + web/wlBadge.css
B: served as static assets from web/ by an existing host (which one?)
items.impact: A needs no extra cards. B or C adds hosting or packaging work the request does not mention.

history.question: How is the badge delivered and consumed? Is it only merged to main of the POC repo for a later client-list slice to import, or must it be served or published somewhere now?

items.answer: Contrast of var(--on-wl) on var(--wl-1..4), computed from web/tokens.css and re-verified by the PM: 6.29, 5.93, 5.93, 8.16 — all ≥ 4.5:1.
items.quote: Text and its background meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (4.5:1 for normal text).

options: Message naming function, allowed values and received value; tests assert only the type

items.source: pm: michael 2026-10-07 — The request fixes only the error type; a descriptive message helps debugging and no contract depends on it

items.question: The brand standard decides colour, typeface, radius and padding but not font size, weight, line-height or display. Should the badge set any of these?
options: Set only what the standard decides, plus display: inline-block and white-space: nowrap; size, weight and line-height inherit from the list (recommended)
Fix a size and weight now (e.g. 12px bold)
items.impact: Changes how the badge looks in the list; no effect on the contract or on contrast.
